mainTopic: Parching and the meaning of כרמל for the עומר, and whether smoothing grain while it is הקדש or owned by a גוי exempts it from מעשרות
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about the פסוק of the עומר, 'אביב קלוי באש גרש כרמל.' It explains that קלי means the grain was parched inside a perforated tube, not thrown straight into the fire. The word באש shows that the whole ear is parched first and ground into groats afterward. כרמל is read as רך ומל, soft and crumbly. This way of reading one word as a short phrase is supported by four more examples: בצקלנו, נתעלסה, נעלסה and ירט. The school of רבי ישמעאל reads כרמל differently, as כר מלא, a full kernel. The גמרא then returns to the משנה, where רבי עקיבא requires חלה and מעשרות from the leftover עומר flour. רב כהנא's reason, that smoothing (מירוח) while the grain is הקדש does not exempt it, is challenged twice and rejected. רבי יוחנן and רבא explain instead that the Temple money paid only for the flour that was needed, and that הקדש smoothing exempts according to everyone. Finally, רבא shows that smoothing by a גוי is a מחלוקת תנאים, from a ברייתא about separating תרומה.

steps.title: קלי does not mean direct fire
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the word קלי does not mean the grain was put straight into the fire. It means a different method, connected to a קליל (polished) vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word קלי does not mean plain fire. It means something else: a polished vessel was used.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the word קלי (parched) from the עומר פסוק. It says the grain was not simply thrown into the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think 'parched' means the grain was held right in the flames. The ברייתא says no: the word points to a different method, and it links קלי to the word קליל, a polished metal vessel. How exactly this worked is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Parched or roasted grain
Fire
Something else, a different meaning
Polished or burnished (metal); here linked to the word קלי

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying fire was not used at all. The grain was still parched by fire, just inside a vessel and not directly in the flames.

phrases.english: Fire is not the meaning of the word 'kali'
rather, it means something else
(How so? etc.)
phrases.notes: These words in round brackets appear in the regular printed גמרא, but the corrected text leaves them out.

phrases.english: The word 'kali' means nothing
other than a (different) polished thing.
phrases.notes: Read it without the bracketed word: 'a קליל thing.' קליל sounds like קלי and means a polished metal vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין אוּר לְשׁוֹן קָלִי אֶלָּא דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קלי in the עומר פסוק does not mean direct fire. It refers to parching by means of a polished vessel.

steps.title: The perforated parching tube
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא describes how the parching was done: a hollow tube full of holes like a sieve, so the fire could reach all the grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did it work? There was a hollow tube for parching grain in the מקדש. It had holes like a sieve, so the fire could reach every part of the grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks 'how so?' and describes the actual tool used to parch the עומר grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fills in step 1. The grain sat inside a tube, so it was not directly in the flames. Because the tube was full of holes, the fire still reached all of it, so the grain really was parched by fire.

keyTerms.meaning: A hollow tube or pipe
Parched grains
Perforated, full of holes
A sieve
Takes hold of, reaches

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the method was both 'in a vessel' and still 'by fire.' That is how the ברייתא fits the word קלי together with the פסוק's word באש.

phrases.english: How so?
There was a hollow tube for parched grain there,
and it was perforated like a sieve,
so that the fire would take hold of all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? אַבּוּב שֶׁל קְלָיוֹת הָיָה שָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains in practical terms the method that step 1 hinted at.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עומר grain was parched in a perforated tube so the fire reached all of it.

steps.title: Is the whole ear parched, or the groats?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a doubt: does 'parched' go with 'ear' (whole grain) or with 'groats' (ground grain)?
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'ear parched with fire, groats.' I don't know whether it means the ear is parched or the groats are parched.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out that the word 'parched' in the פסוק could describe either of two words. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists אביב (fresh ear), קלוי (parched), and גרש (groats). Grammatically, 'parched' could describe the whole grain before grinding or the groats after grinding. This decides the order of the process: parch first and then grind, or grind first and then parch.

keyTerms.meaning: Fresh ripe grain, still in the ear
Groats, coarsely ground grain
Parched

phrases.english: 'Grain in the ear parched ... groats,'
I do not know whether it means 'parched ear'
or 'parched groats,'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם אָבִיב קָלוּי אִם גֶּרֶשׂ קָלוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what קלי means to which word in the פסוק it describes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does קלוי describe the אביב (before grinding) or the גרש (after grinding)?

steps.title: The word 'with fire' separates the phrases
steps.stepSummary: The word באש breaks the פסוק into two parts, so 'parched' goes with the ear, not the groats.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says 'with fire,' it cuts off the phrase. So 'parched with fire' goes with the ear, and 'groats' starts a new part.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the doubt. The word באש acts like a break in the sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since באש comes between קלוי and גרש, it closes the phrase 'אביב קלוי באש.' So the whole ear is parched first, and only afterward is it ground into groats.

keyTerms.meaning: With fire
It broke off the matter; it separates one phrase from the next

steps.whatToRemember: The order for the עומר is: parch the whole ear first, then grind it into groats. We know this because באש separates the two phrases.

phrases.english: When it says 'with fire'
it broke off the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: באש ends the phrase, so קלוי describes the אביב (the whole ear), not the groats.

steps.title: כרמל means soft and crumbly
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads the word כרמל as a short form of 'רך ומל', soft and easily crumbled.
steps.simpleTranslation: כרמל means soft and crumbly.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the last word of the עומר פסוק, כרמל, by splitting it into two words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כרמל is read as רך (soft) plus מל (crumbly). This tells us the עומר grain was fresh and moist, soft enough to crumble easily. The next steps bring other פסוקים where a single word is read as a short form of a longer phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: Fresh, moist grain
Soft
Crumbly, easily rubbed apart

phrases.english: 'Karmel'
means soft and crumbly,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: כרמל is read as רך ומל: the עומר grain is soft and crumbly.

steps.title: Support from the sack brought to אלישע
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes a פסוק in מלכים ב that has כרמל next to the word בצקלנו. It reads בצקלנו as a short form of a whole phrase, showing that this kind of reading is used elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, the פסוק says: 'A man came from בעל שלשה and brought the man of God bread of first fruits, twenty barley loaves, and fresh grain in his sack. He said: Give it to the people to eat.' 'In his sack' is read as: he came, poured for us, we ate, and it was fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק that uses the word כרמל, and in the same פסוק it reads another word, בצקלנו, as a short form of a longer phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up the reading כרמל = רך ומל by showing the same method on בצקלנו. The ברייתא reads it as בא (he came), יצק לנו (poured for us), אכלנו (we ate), נוה היה (it was fine). So reading one word as a short phrase is a known way of explaining פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: In his sack; here read as a short form of a whole phrase
Poured
Fine, pleasant
Bread of first fruits

phrases.english: And similarly it says:
'And a man came from Baal Shalishah'
and brought the man of God bread of first fruits,
twenty loaves of barley,
and fresh grain in his sack,
and he said: Give to the people, and let them eat,'
He came and poured for us, and we ate,
phrases.notes: This is the word בצקלנו broken into pieces: ב for בא, צק for יצק, ל for לנו, and נ for נוה in the next line.

phrases.english: and it was fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 5's way of reading a word as a short form of a phrase.
steps.raayaObject: The method of reading one word (like כרמל) as a short form of a longer phrase
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 4:42, where בצקלנו is read as בא ויצק לנו ואכלנו ונוה היה

steps.title: Another example: נתעלסה in משלי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds another example. The word נתעלסה in משלי is read as a short form of a string of words.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'Let us delight ourselves with love.' נתעלסה means: we will talk, go up, rejoice, and be pampered with love.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives one more example of a single word read as a short form of a longer phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נתעלסה is broken into letters that start other words: נשא ונתן (talk together), נעלה (go up), נשמח (rejoice), נתחטא (be pampered). A second example strengthens the idea that this method is used in פסוקים, which supports the reading of כרמל.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us delight ourselves; here read as a short form of a phrase
Literally 'carry and give'; here it means to talk together
Be pampered, indulge ourselves
Love

steps.whatToRemember: כרמל = רך ומל. The ברייתא supports reading one word as a short phrase with two other examples: בצקלנו and נתעלסה.

phrases.english: And it says: 'Let us delight ourselves with love,'
we will converse, and we will go up,
and we will rejoice and be pampered with love.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second supporting example to the one in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The method of reading one word as a short form of a longer phrase
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 7:18, where נתעלסה is read as נשא ונתן ונעלה ונשמח ונתחטא

steps.title: Another shortened word: נעלסה in איוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a third example of a word read as a short form of several words. The word נעלסה is read as 'carries, goes up, settles down.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'The wing of the ostrich beats joyously (נעלסה).' This means: carries, goes up, and settles down.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more example to show that reading one word as several words is a normal way of reading פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 used נתעלסה from משלי. Now a similar word, נעלסה from איוב, is broken into the letters of three words: נושא (carries), עולה (goes up), and נתחטא (settles). Each new example makes it more convincing that כרמל can be read as רך ומל.

keyTerms.meaning: The wing of the ostrich (a bird in איוב)
Beats joyously; here read as three words
Carries
And settles down

phrases.english: And it says: "The wing of the ostrich beats joyously,"
carries, goes up, and settles down.
phrases.notes: The bird carries its egg, flies up, and settles it in its nest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further example after נתעלסה, supporting the same reading method.
steps.raayaObject: That כרמל can be read as a short form of רך ומל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 39:13, where נעלסה is read as נושא, עולה, ונתחטא.

steps.title: Another shortened word: ירט in the story of בלעם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a last example. The word ירט is read as 'she feared, she saw, she turned aside,' describing בלעם's donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'For your way is contrary (ירט) against me.' This means: she feared, she saw, she turned aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of examples with the word ירט from the story of בלעם's donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter of ירט is taken from a word: י from יראתה (she feared), ר from ראתה (she saw), and ט from נטתה (she turned aside). This is the same method used for כרמל, so it gives the reading one more support.

keyTerms.meaning: Contrary; here read as three words
She feared
She turned aside

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא reads כרמל as רך ומל, and backs this up with other words read the same way: בצקלנו, נתעלסה, נעלסה, and ירט.

phrases.english: And it says: "For your way is contrary against me"
phrases.notes: במדבר 22:32, the angel speaking to בלעם about his donkey.

phrases.english: she feared, she saw, she turned aside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last example in the same list of shortened words.
steps.raayaObject: That reading a word as a short form of several words is an accepted method, supporting רך ומל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 22:32, where ירט is read as יראתה, ראתה, נטתה.

steps.title: A different reading of כרמל: a full kernel
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads כרמל as כר מלא, 'a full kernel.' This is a different explanation from רך ומל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: כרמל means 'a full kernel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second way to explain the word כרמל, taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, כרמל was read as רך ומל, soft and easily crumbled. Here the word is split into כר (kernel) and מלא (full), meaning grain whose husk is filled with a ripe kernel. Both readings treat כרמל as a combination of words, but they describe the grain differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the פסוק about the new grain offering
A kernel (here, the husk holding the grain)
Full

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Karmel" means a full kernel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of כרמל, next to the ברייתא's רך ומל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כרמל means כר מלא, a full kernel.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי עקיבא obligates חלה and מעשרות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה again: רבי עקיבא holds that the leftover flour must have חלה and מעשרות taken from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא obligates it in חלה and in מעשרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a new line in the משנה, quoting רבי עקיבא's opinion. This sets up the next step, where רב כהנא explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה deals with the leftover flour of the עומר, which is redeemed and may be eaten. The first opinion obligates it in חלה but exempts it from מעשרות. רבי עקיבא disagrees and obligates it in both, so the גמרא now needs to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligates, holds that it must
The portion of dough given to a כהן
Tithes taken from produce

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva obligates it
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. "It" means the leftover flour of the עומר.

phrases.english: in challah and in the tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of כרמל and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the leftover flour is obligated in both חלה and מעשרות.

steps.title: רב כהנא explains: smoothing while הקדש does not exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains רבי עקיבא's reason: if grain was smoothed into a pile while it was הקדש, that does not exempt it from מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: רבי עקיבא used to say: smoothing grain that is הקדש does not exempt it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives the reason behind רבי עקיבא's opinion in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smoothing the grain pile (מירוח) is normally the moment that makes מעשרות required. The other view says that since the smoothing happened while the grain was הקדש, the grain is exempt even after it is redeemed. רבי עקיבא says smoothing while הקדש does not cancel the obligation, so after redemption the flour still needs מעשרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Smoothing the grain pile, the step that makes מעשרות required
Property that belongs to the בית המקדש
Exempts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying הקדש grain needs מעשרות while it is still הקדש. The point is that once it is redeemed, the earlier smoothing does not free it from מעשרות.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: מירוח הקדש אינו פוטר. Smoothing done while the grain was הקדש does not exempt it from מעשרות after it is redeemed.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Rabbi Akiva would say:
The smoothing of consecrated grain does not exempt it.
phrases.notes: He means it does not exempt it from מעשרות once the grain is redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבי עקיבא's opinion quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי עקיבא obligate the leftover flour in מעשרות?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because in his view, smoothing done while the grain was הקדש does not exempt it.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא about the leftover barley
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a ברייתא to challenge רב כהנא. In it, the חכמים argue against רבי עקיבא from the case of someone who redeems produce from the Temple treasurer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת challenges: What did they do with the leftover of these three סאין? It is redeemed and anyone may eat it. It owes חלה but is exempt from מעשרות. רבי עקיבא says it owes both חלה and מעשרות. The חכמים answered him: someone who redeems produce from the Temple treasurer proves the point, since he owes חלה but is exempt from מעשרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב כהנא. רב ששת first quotes the ברייתא, and in the next step he will explain what the problem is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows the חכמים trying to prove their view to רבי עקיבא from a known case. That case is produce bought back from the גזבר, which is exempt from מעשרות. Their argument only works if רבי עקיבא already agrees about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover: the barley flour not used for the עומר offering
סאה measures; three סאין of barley were harvested for the עומר
It is redeemed, bought back from הקדש so it becomes ordinary food
The Temple treasurer who handles הקדש property
Will prove: a case brought as proof for an argument

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raises an objection:
The leftover of these three se'a,
what would they do with it?
It is redeemed and eaten by any person,
and it is obligated in challah, and exempt from tithes.
Rabbi Akiva obligates it in challah and in tithes.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: פּוֹדֶה מִיַּד גִּזְבָּר יוֹכִיחַ,
phrases.english: They said to him: one who redeems from the hand of the treasurer will prove it,
that he is obligated in challah and exempt from tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to challenge רב כהנא's explanation in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that, for רבי עקיבא, smoothing grain while it is הקדש does not exempt it from מעשרות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source is quoted here. The attack itself is spelled out in step 14.

steps.title: The חכמים's proof would be pointless under רב כהנא's view
steps.stepSummary: If רבי עקיבא held that smoothing grain in הקדש does not exempt it, then the גזבר case is exactly what he disagrees about. So it could not serve as a proof against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is true that smoothing grain while it is הקדש does not exempt it, what were the חכמים telling him? That case is the very same thing!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains his challenge. The חכמים's argument only makes sense if רבי עקיבא agrees that produce redeemed from the גזבר is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce redeemed from the גזבר was smoothed into a pile while it was הקדש. If רבי עקיבא thought such smoothing does not exempt, he would say that case is obligated too. Then the חכמים would have proved nothing. Since they brought it as a proof, רבי עקיבא must agree it is exempt, and so רב כהנא's reason cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Smoothing the pile of grain; the step that creates the obligation of מעשרות
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
If it is so: introduces the view being tested
It is the very same: the proof is the same as the point in dispute

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב ששת is arguing with רבי עקיבא's ruling. He is attacking only רב כהנא's explanation of WHY רבי עקיבא rules this way.

phrases.english: And if it is so
that smoothing while it is consecrated does not exempt,
what are they saying to him?
It is the very same!
phrases.notes: He means the case of redeeming from the גזבר is exactly what רבי עקיבא would argue about, so it cannot be used to prove anything to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא דְּמֵירוּחַ הֶקְדֵּשׁ אֵינוֹ פּוֹטֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the problem with the ברייתא quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים use the גזבר case as an accepted proof. That only works if רבי עקיבא agrees that smoothing in הקדש exempts, which contradicts רב כהנא.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives רבי עקיבא a different reason
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא בר תחליפא quotes a ברייתא. It says רבי עקיבא's reason is that the הקדש money paid only for the flour that was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, רב כהנא בר תחליפא challenged רב כהנא: רבי עקיבא requires חלה and מעשרות because the money was given only for what they needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב כהנא. A ברייתא states openly that רבי עקיבא's reason is something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says only the needed amount was paid for with Temple money. So the leftover was never truly הקדש, and it was smoothed as ordinary produce. This implies that if all of it had really been הקדש, it would be exempt, which contradicts רב כהנא.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: introduces an additional challenge
Money, here the Temple funds used to buy the barley for the עומר
For the need: only for the portion actually required

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא
phrases.english: And furthermore, Rav Kahana bar Tachlifa raised an objection
to Rav Kahana (bar Matitya):
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some leave them out. Either way, this is the רב כהנא from step 12.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva obligates in challah and in tithes,
because the money was not given
except for what they needed.
phrases.notes: Only the flour actually used for the עומר was paid for with Temple money. The rest was never truly הקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא לְרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate challenge against רב כהנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's explanation of רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא names a different reason, one that only makes sense if smoothing in הקדש would normally exempt.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן gives the accepted reason
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא's explanation is set aside. רבי יוחנן says רבי עקיבא had a settled tradition that the Temple money covered only the needed portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: It is a settled tradition in the mouth of רבי עקיבא that the money was given only for what they needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב כהנא's reason and replaces it with רבי יוחנן's. The leftover was never really bought by הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the earlier explanation is rejected. רבי עקיבא agrees that smoothing in הקדש exempts from מעשרות. But the leftover barley was not הקדש when it was smoothed, so it owes מעשרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier explanation and gives a new one
A settled, well-arranged tradition that is firmly held

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא obligates the leftover עומר flour in מעשרות not because smoothing in הקדש fails to exempt. The reason is that the Temple paid only for the needed portion, so the rest was never הקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי עקיבא and the חכמים agree on the basic rule that smoothing in הקדש exempts. They argue only about whether the leftover barley was ever הקדש.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד עָרוּךְ הוּא בְּפִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: It is a settled tradition in the mouth of Rabbi Akiva,
that the money was not given
except for what they needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב כהנא's rejected reason with the reason found in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי עקיבא requires מעשרות from the leftover flour (asked in step 11).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Temple money paid only for the needed flour, so the leftover was never הקדש and was smoothed as ordinary produce.

steps.title: Smoothing grain while it is הקדש exempts it
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it is obvious that מירוח done while grain is הקדש exempts it from מעשרות. Even רבי עקיבא agrees; he required tithing only in the עומר case, because there the money paid only for the needed flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: To me it is obvious that smoothing grain while it belongs to הקדש exempts it. Even רבי עקיבא required tithing there only because the Temple money paid just for what was needed. But in general, smoothing done while the grain is הקדש exempts it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds on the conclusion of step 16. He states a clear rule: grain smoothed while it was הקדש does not need מעשרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא had thought רבי עקיבא held that הקדש smoothing does not exempt, and that idea was rejected. רבא now says the opposite is so clear that everyone agrees. רבי עקיבא's ruling in the עומר case comes from a special reason: the leftover grain never really belonged to הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious to me
Smoothing the grain into a pile; the final stage of processing that makes produce obligated in מעשרות
Property that belongs to the Temple
Exempts
In general; in an ordinary case

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the baseline: הקדש smoothing exempts. רבא can now move to the harder question about smoothing done by a גוי.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is obvious to me
that smoothing while consecrated exempts,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לָא קָא מְחַיֵּיב הָתָם
phrases.english: and even Rabbi Akiva only obligates there
phrases.notes: "There" means the leftover barley of the עומר from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: because the money was given only
for what was needed for them,
but smoothing while consecrated, in general, exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical rule from רבי יוחנן's explanation in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smoothing done while grain is הקדש exempts it from מעשרות, according to everyone, including רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Smoothing by a גוי is a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that whether מירוח done by a גוי exempts the grain is a מחלוקת between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Smoothing done by a גוי is a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא moves to a second case: grain that was smoothed while a גוי owned it. He says it is a מחלוקת תנאים. This line sets up the ברייתא that will prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the הקדש case, this one is not obvious. רבא claims that תנאים disagree about it. The next steps bring the source that shows the two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים, the sages of the משנה period
Smoothing done while the grain belonged to a non-Jew

phrases.english: Smoothing by a gentile is a dispute of Tannaim,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the clear הקדש case to the disputed case of a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether smoothing by a גוי exempts the grain depends on a מחלוקת תנאים.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה: one may separate תרומה across all groups
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא first brings רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. They allow separating תרומה from the produce of anyone for the produce of anyone: ישראל, גוים, or כותים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: One separates תרומה from a ישראל's produce for a ישראל's produce, from גוים' produce for גוים' produce, and from כותים' produce for כותים' produce. One may even separate from anyone's produce for anyone's produce. These are the words of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings the first side of the ברייתא to prove his claim. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה treat all this produce the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you can separate from a ישראל's produce for a גוי's produce, both must carry the same obligation. So these תנאים hold that smoothing by a גוי does not exempt the grain. It is obligated just like a ישראל's produce.

keyTerms.meaning: One separates תרומה
Samaritans
From anyone's produce for anyone's produce

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says the word מירוח. רבא reads it as a proof about מירוח: if the produce can be mixed and matched, it must all have the same obligation.

phrases.english: As it is taught: One separates teruma from that of a Jew
for that of a Jew,
and from that of gentiles for that of gentiles,
phrases.notes: He means produce that was smoothed while gentiles owned it and that is now in front of us to be tithed.

phrases.english: and from that of Samaritans for that of Samaritans,
and from that of anyone for that of anyone,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: תּוֹרְמִין מִשֶּׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבא's claim in step 18, starting with the first opinion.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that smoothing by a גוי is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה allow separating תרומה across all groups, which shows that a גוי's smoothing does not exempt.

steps.title: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון: no crossing between a ישראל's produce and a גוי's
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון allow separating within a ישראל's produce, and between גוים' and כותים' produce. They do not allow crossing between a ישראל's produce and that of גוים or כותים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: One separates תרומה from a ישראל's produce for a ישראל's produce. One may also separate from גוים' produce for כותים' produce, and from כותים' produce for גוים' produce. But one may not separate from a ישראל's produce for that of גוים or כותים. Nor may one separate from that of גוים or כותים for a ישראל's produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון split the produce into two separate groups that cannot be mixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They put גוים and כותים in one group and ישראל in another. They forbid separating from one group for the other. That shows they hold the produce of a גוי or כותי has a different status: smoothing by a גוי exempts it. With both sides in place, רבא's claim of a מחלוקת תנאים is proven.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of גוים and of כותים, treated here as one group
But not; this marks where the limit is set
Nor; the limit works in the other direction too

steps.whatToRemember: הקדש smoothing exempts according to everyone. Smoothing by a גוי depends on a מחלוקת. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say it does not exempt, so all the produce can be mixed. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say it exempts, so a ישראל's produce cannot be mixed with a גוי's.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹרְמִין מִשֶּׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: One separates teruma from that of a Jew for that of a Jew,
and from that of gentiles for that of Samaritans,
and from that of Samaritans for that of gentiles,
but not from that of a Jew
for that of gentiles or of Samaritans,
nor from that of gentiles or of Samaritans
for that of a Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא, which completes the proof that there is a מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that smoothing by a גוי is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: In the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid crossing between a ישראל's produce and a גוי's or כותי's. This shows they hold a גוי's smoothing exempts.
